correctness.rationale: Odd Kneser graph KG(2k+1,k) has no 4-cycle: two different k-subsets share at most one disjoint k-neighbor. Every Hom cell has a singleton coordinate; contractible star-cover simplices intersect only in points corresponding to ordered disjoint pairs. Equivariant nerve is connected bipartite D_k with 2*C(2k+1,k) vertices and (k+1)*C(2k+1,k) edges, so H1 is its integral oriented cycle kernel of rank (k-1)*C(2k+1,k)+1, with swap reversing edge orientation. Decomposing ordered edges as Ind_{S_2k}^{S_(2k+1)} M^(k,k), complement sends two-row Specht S^(2k-j,j) to (-1)^j; the Pieri rule adds one box, all two-row terms cancel against H0 and the vertex representation, leaving exactly three-row S^(2k-j,j,1) with swap sign (-1)^(j+1). Fixed-chain trace yields 1-2^r precisely for one fixed point and all other cycles even, otherwise 1. Inspected program independently computes Frobenius-alternant characters of all cycle types k=2..5; did not interpret these finite tests as the unrestricted proof.
residual_risks: A prior implicit equivariant induction calculation or unindexed Kneser box-complex representation may cover the Specht formula.
The general integral graph-cycle kernel follows from known square-free nerve results and is not itself novel.
Finite k character tables are corroboration, not proof for all k.
